# Project Governance 4.0.0

The major release makes implementation tracking and focused linting deterministic, and makes
context quality and observed task costs inspectable through the existing runtime.

- Versioned Markdown plans provide stable batch/item IDs, compact inspection and exact targeted
  progress updates. Verification uses original check evidence. Failed, unrelated, stale or
  zero-work checks cannot complete verification. Historical unavailable proof remains visible.
- A structured specification template distinguishes mechanical checks from acceptance judgment.
  Plan links bind the whole specification; a passing check cannot certify arbitrary prose.
- Focused lint setup preserves existing rules and required coverage. Qualified Ruff and ESLint
  adapters read captured source/configuration, including staged inputs, and distinguish findings
  from infrastructure failures. Checking never installs tools or silently creates a debt baseline.
- Release evaluation joins exact runtime generations, task revisions, native/provider outcomes,
  context decisions and observed usage. Missing acceptance, cost or host observation stays unknown.
- Frozen context-quality cases inspect discovery, descriptor submission, passage judgment and
  complete final evidence. Complete negative advice may omit automatic unpinned optional originals;
  required, explicit, partial, uncertain or conflicting evidence retains conservative fallback.
- Multilingual review captures Kotlin, Swift and Python alongside JavaScript/TypeScript. Frozen
  known-fault cases characterize JEV advice separately from actual executed behavior.
- An explicit long-check-log pilot keeps failures, results, cleanup and original references in
  code. JEV selects only optional routine material. Default output does not activate the pilot.
- Installed journey regressions cover greenfield work, read-only consultation, batch-before-review,
  linked worktrees and synthetic same-session continuation through a generation change.

Adoption is deliberate. Existing projects, pins and native conversations are not changed by
publication. Structured plans and lint setup require explicit adoption. Coding models remain fixed;
JEV cannot authorize work, waive checks, establish acceptance or initiate delegation.

Qualification uses local source tests, exact installed archives, real local lint tools, independent
review and separately labelled live JEV synthetic cases. Synthetic host events do not prove desktop
reattachment. Live advice is experimental; no accepted-task token savings or universal semantic
accuracy is claimed. Unsupported delivery-before-read and extra-read observations remain unknown.

This is an operator-authorized manual release. Hosted CI is not part of this qualification.
